topic: MCP Snoop Review 2026: Wireshark for MCP — Transparent Proxy for Tool Call Debugging

key_points: Transparent stdio shim — wraps any MCP server command, sits in the real data path between client and server
Live TUI with Bubble Tea — real-time frame inspection, filtering, drill-down
Dual-role architecture: shim (stdio forwarder + frame copier) and hub (TUI + session store)
Supports stdio mode (mcpsnoop -- <server>) and HTTP reverse proxy mode (mcpsnoop http --target <url>)
Session export to JSON, HTML, text, and OTLP (OpenTelemetry) for tracing backends
CI check mode — gates on errors, invalid frames, warnings, slow calls, pending calls
Remote SSH tunnel support for watching sessions on another machine
Secret redaction — key-based, JSONPath-based, and regex-based value scrubbing
Config file support (.mcpsnoop.toml) for reusable shim flags
Written in Go, single binary, no runtime dependencies
270 GitHub stars, MIT license, created June 2026, very active development (v0.9.0 by July 15)
Keybindings: filter by tool/method/id/direction/kind/status, replay calls, inspect capabilities, export sessions
Official MCP Inspector — testing and evaluation platform for MCP servers
2068 stars — most popular MCP debugging tool
Web-based UI for chatting, inspecting, and debugging MCP servers
Connects as its own client — does NOT see real client-server traffic
Supports OAuth, evals, CI/CD integration
TypeScript, created May 2025, broader scope (includes ChatGPT app testing)
MCP debugging proxy and CLI inspection tool
125 stars, TypeScript, MIT license
Created June 2025 — more mature project
CLI-focused debugging proxy for MCP traffic
Debug MCP requests in real-time via proxy URL
7 stars, TypeScript, created June 2025
Point your MCP client at a proxy URL and watch traffic flow
Lightweight, focused on request interception
Drop-in MCP proxy for debugging AI agents
4 stars, Rust, Apache-2.0, created April 2026
Real-time timeline, replay, diff capabilities
Local-first, no telemetry, single binary
Similar positioning to mcpsnoop but much smaller community

stats.fact: mcpsnoop reached 270 GitHub stars within 3 weeks of its first release (June 27 – July 16, 2026)
mcpsnoop has 18 forks and 2 open issues as of July 16, 2026
mcpsnoop released 9 versions (v0.1.0 through v0.9.0) in 18 days, showing rapid iteration
MCP Inspector (MCPJam/inspector) has 2068 stars — the dominant MCP debugging tool
mcpsnoop's Show HN post on Hacker News received 64 points and 22 comments
reloaderoo has 125 stars as the second most popular dedicated MCP debugging proxy
mcpsnoop is written in Go with Bubble Tea TUI framework, producing a single binary with no runtime deps
The MCP ecosystem has at least 6+ dedicated debugging/proxy tools (mcpsnoop, reloaderoo, mcp-interceptor, mcpobservatory, MCP Inspector, HyprMCP)

angles: mcpsnoop's key differentiator: it sits in the REAL data path, unlike MCP Inspector which connects as its own client and never sees actual client-server traffic
The 'Wireshark for MCP' positioning is apt — it's a transparent proxy that captures every JSON-RPC frame live, like Wireshark captures network packets
Rapid development velocity (9 releases in 18 days) signals strong community interest and active maintenance
Unique features no competitor has: CI check mode, OTLP export, SSH remote tunnel, secret redaction, replay capability
The tool addresses a real pain point: 'When a tool silently isn't called, capabilities don't line up, or a call just hangs, you're left digging through logs and guessing'
Comparison table in README directly positions against MCP Inspector on 10 dimensions — mcpsnoop wins on all of them
Growing ecosystem of MCP debugging tools indicates MCP adoption is accelerating and developers need better observability
